questions.stem: In contrast with POC, Prototype and Pilot/MVP, what is prepared and used in the productionised solution stage?
options: A subset of data on limited hardware
Dummy data on a developer laptop
Complete infrastructure, software and data
Only the semantic layer
A single server with a single licence
questions.explanation: In the productionised solution stage a complete infrastructure, software and data are prepared and used.

questions.stem: What does UT stand for and who performs it?
options: Unit Testing, done by the developer during development for every piece of code
User Testing, done by business users after go-live
Usability Testing, done by the design team
Upgrade Testing, done by the vendor
Uptime Testing, done by operations
questions.explanation: UT stands for Unit Testing and is done by the developer during the development phase for every piece of code developed.

options: Security Integration Testing
Systems Integration Testing
Standard Interface Testing
Software Installation Testing
Statistical Inference Testing
questions.explanation: SIT stands for Systems Integration Testing.

questions.stem: How does a SIT environment compare in size with the actual solution?
options: It must be identical in size to Production
It must be larger than Production to stress test
It has no components of the actual solution
It has all the possible components but is small in size, for example 1 server and 1 licence instead of 10 servers and 100 licences
It exists only on paper
questions.explanation: The SIT environment has all the possible components of the actual solution but is small in size; if Production needs 10 servers and 100 licences, SIT can run with 1 server and 1 licence.

options: That top management approves the dashboards
That the sales forecast is accurate
That the marketing campaign is ready
That the budget has been signed
That code runs end to end, user access is set, security protocols are in place and job dependencies are in place
questions.explanation: In SIT, we make sure the code can run end to end, user access is properly set, security protocols are in place and job dependencies are in place.

questions.stem: Why is dropping SIT to save cost described as a bad idea?
options: Because SIT is the first step cut to save cost, yet it is NOT a good idea, and newcomers may soon not even know what SIT is
Because SIT is required by law
Because SIT replaces UAT entirely
Because SIT is the only place where developers write code
Because SIT costs nothing
questions.explanation: SIT is disappearing because it is the first step cut to save cost, which is not a good idea; in a decade newcomers might not even know what SIT is.

questions.stem: What should a UAT environment ideally look like, and what data does it use?
options: Like a developer laptop, with dummy data
Like Production, using anonymised or synthetic data of actual production size
Like the POC, with no data
Like a spreadsheet, with sample rows
Like an archive, with historical data only
questions.explanation: The UAT environment should ideally look like Production, using anonymised or synthetic but actual-size data so business users can test before release.

questions.stem: When does UAT come into the picture?
options: Before any code is written
Before unit testing
After SIT is successful
After the solution goes live
During the POC
questions.explanation: UAT comes into the picture after SIT is a success.

questions.stem: What must the Production environment comply with?
options: Only the developers' coding standards
Only the sales team's timeline
Only internal style guides
Internal compliance and audit requirements as well as external regulatory bodies' standards
Nothing, since Production is the final version
questions.explanation: The production environment must comply with internal compliance and audit requirements as well as external regulatory bodies' standards.

questions.stem: Which of the following is NOT part of the productionised solution stage after a successful MVP?
options: Gathering complete business requirements and making a complete design
Building teams and making a project plan
Signing an end-to-end SOW
Conducting UT, SIT and UAT before going live
Using only a subset of real data and limited features
questions.explanation: Using a subset of data and limited features describes the MVP; the productionised stage gathers complete requirements, designs fully, signs the SOW, tests with UT, SIT and UAT, and goes live with complete data.
